-- | Distinct session, physical-window and physical-pane IDs.
--
-- Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries no endpoint, server lifetime
-- or liveness evidence. Render an ID for external text; use its numeric
-- accessor when an application needs the mathematical value.
--
-- Start with 'parseSessionId', 'parseWindowId' or 'parsePaneId'. Each type's
-- documentation links its parser and renderer. Contextual numeric indices
-- belong to "LibTmux.Value".
--
-- >>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
-- >>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
-- Right "@17"
-- >>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")
-- "rejected"
module LibTmux.Id
  ( -- * Entity identities
    SessionId
  , WindowId
  , PaneId
    -- * Parse external values
  , IdError (..)
  , parseSessionId
  , parseWindowId
  , parsePaneId
    -- * Render target text
  , renderSessionId
  , renderWindowId
  , renderPaneId
    -- * Read numeric values
  , sessionIdValue
  , windowIdValue
  , paneIdValue
  ) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData)
import Control.Monad (guard)
import Data.Char (ord)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import Data.Word (Word32)

-- | A session's unsigned 32-bit tmux identifier, written with a @$@ prefix.
-- Parse with 'parseSessionId'; render with 'renderSessionId'.
newtype SessionId = SessionId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | A physical window's identifier, independent of its session links.
-- Parse with 'parseWindowId'; render with 'renderWindowId'.
newtype WindowId = WindowId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | A physical pane's identifier, written with a @%@ prefix.
-- Parse with 'parsePaneId'; render with 'renderPaneId'.
newtype PaneId = PaneId Word32
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | Invalid canonical syntax, entity prefix or native unsigned range.
-- Diagnostics retain at most 64 characters of input.
data IdError = InvalidId
  { expectedPrefix :: !Char -- ^ Required entity prefix.
  , input :: !Text -- ^ Bounded copy of the invalid input.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Parse @$0@ through @$4294967295@. No whitespace or leading zeroes.
parseSessionId :: Text -> Either IdError SessionId
parseSessionId = fmap SessionId . parseId '$'

-- | Parse a canonical @\@number@ identifying a physical window.
parseWindowId :: Text -> Either IdError WindowId
parseWindowId = fmap WindowId . parseId '@'

-- | Parse a canonical @%number@ identifying a physical pane.
parsePaneId :: Text -> Either IdError PaneId
parsePaneId = fmap PaneId . parseId '%'

-- | Render the session prefix and decimal ID.
renderSessionId :: SessionId -> Text
renderSessionId (SessionId value) = "$" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Render the physical window prefix and decimal ID.
renderWindowId :: WindowId -> Text
renderWindowId (WindowId value) = "@" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Render the physical pane prefix and decimal ID.
renderPaneId :: PaneId -> Text
renderPaneId (PaneId value) = "%" <> Text.pack (show value)

-- | Read the numeric session ID without narrowing conversion.
sessionIdValue :: SessionId -> Integer
sessionIdValue (SessionId value) = toInteger value

-- | Read the numeric physical window ID.
windowIdValue :: WindowId -> Integer
windowIdValue (WindowId value) = toInteger value

-- | Read the numeric physical pane ID.
paneIdValue :: PaneId -> Integer
paneIdValue (PaneId value) = toInteger value

parseId :: Char -> Text -> Either IdError Word32
parseId prefix input = maybe invalid Right parsed
  where
    invalid = Left (InvalidId prefix (Text.copy (Text.take 64 input)))
    parsed = do
      guard (Text.length input <= 11)
      (actual, digits) <- Text.uncons input
      guard (actual == prefix)
      (first, rest) <- Text.uncons digits
      guard (first /= '0' || Text.null rest)
      guard (Text.all (\c -> c >= '0' && c <= '9') digits)
      let value = Text.foldl' (\n c -> n * 10 + toInteger (ord c - ord '0')) 0 digits
      guard (value <= toInteger (maxBound @Word32))
      pure (fromInteger value)

-- | Typed selection over detached tmux observations.
--
-- Build a t'Query' with a source and 'matching', then use 'runQuery' to read
-- an existing t'Snapshot' without IO. 'fetch' explicitly acquires a new
-- snapshot. Ordinary lists and application predicates remain available
-- through "LibTmux.Snapshot"; portable expressions contain no callbacks.
--
-- Import field modules qualified: "LibTmux.Query.Pane",
-- "LibTmux.Query.Session", "LibTmux.Query.Window", "LibTmux.Query.Link",
-- "LibTmux.Query.Occurrence", "LibTmux.Query.Client",
-- "LibTmux.Query.ClientAttachment" and "LibTmux.Query.ServerInfo".
-- Field tokens describe captured values; reading them never contacts tmux.
--
-- Query construction, operands and results are finite. Execution validates
-- every declared requirement before filtering, stably ordering and limiting.
-- The default source order and multiplicity come from the supplied snapshot.
-- A result establishes what was observed, not current liveness or a reserved
-- command target. See 'exactlyOne' before selecting an explicit reference.
--
-- >>> exactlyOne [1 :: Integer]
-- Right 1
-- >>> exactlyOne ([] :: [Integer])
-- Left NoMatches
-- >>> atMostOne ([] :: [Integer])
-- Right Nothing
-- >>> atMostOne [1, 2 :: Integer]
-- Left AtLeastTwoMatches
--
module LibTmux.Query
  ( -- * Descriptions
    Field, Expr, Query, Order, ToMany, ToOne, ToOptional
    -- * Ordered sources
  , sessions, windows, panes, windowLinks, paneOccurrences, clients, serverInfo
    -- * Scalar predicates
  , eq, oneOf, contains, ge, gt, le, lt
  , dimensionAtLeast, dimensionAtMost, paneIndexAtLeast, paneIndexAtMost
  , windowIndexAtLeast, windowIndexAtMost
    -- * Logic and relationships
  , allOf, anyOf, not_, some, every, none, related, optionalRelated
    -- * Selection and ordering
  , matching, orderBy, ascending, descending, limit
    -- * Inspect and evaluate
  , QueryRequirements (..), requirements, QueryError (..), runQuery, fetch
    -- * Cardinality
  , CardinalityError (..), exactlyOne, atMostOne
  ) where

import LibTmux.Internal.Field (Field)
import LibTmux.Internal.Query
  ( Expr, Query, Order, ToMany, ToOne, ToOptional
  , sessions, windows, panes, windowLinks, paneOccurrences, clients, serverInfo
  , eq, oneOf, contains, ge, gt, le, lt
  , dimensionAtLeast, dimensionAtMost, paneIndexAtLeast, paneIndexAtMost
  , windowIndexAtLeast, windowIndexAtMost
  , allOf, anyOf, not_, some, every, none, related, optionalRelated
  , matching, orderBy, ascending, descending, limit
  , QueryRequirements (..), requirements, QueryError (..)
  , CardinalityError (..), exactlyOne, atMostOne
  )
import LibTmux.Internal.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Server (Server)
import LibTmux.Server qualified as Server
import LibTmux.Snapshot (Snapshot)

-- | Validate and evaluate against the supplied complete snapshot. Every
-- requirement is checked before reading rows, including empty sources and
-- zero limits. Consuming a successful result performs only pure processing
-- of owned observations. No acquisition, pushdown or refresh occurs.
runQuery :: Snapshot -> Query row -> Either QueryError [row]
runQuery = Q.runQuery

-- | Acquire a complete fresh snapshot and evaluate the query against it.
-- Compiled evaluator support is checked before IO; version requirements are
-- checked against acquired server metadata. Operational failures propagate
-- as exceptions from 'LibTmux.Server.capture'; use 'LibTmux.Server.tryTmux' to retain their
-- context and recovery owners. Cancellation propagates unchanged.
--
-- This performs one acquisition per call, even when the query is reused or
-- has a zero limit. Use 'runQuery' to reuse an existing t'Snapshot'. No filter
-- is pushed into tmux in this implementation.
fetch :: Server -> Query row -> IO (Either QueryError [row])
fetch server query = case Q.prepare Q.nativeProfile query of
  Left problem -> pure (Left problem)
  Right () -> (`runQuery` query) <$> Server.capture server

-- | Observe and change an existing tmux daemon through an owned Server handle.
--
-- A t'Server' represents one adoption of one endpoint. 'withServer' owns its
-- socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers. Closing this scope
-- releases those resources; it does not send @kill-server@. The tmux noun
-- @Client@ refers to detached observations in "LibTmux.Snapshot".
-- 'withRuntime' and 'withServerIn' give several handles shared resource limits
-- and independent Server scopes. 'withOwnedServer' starts a daemon of its own
-- and retires it with the scope; 'killServer' retires an adopted daemon.
--
-- 'capture' returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph
-- navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic
-- transaction over tmux and operating-system state.
-- 'createSession' returns historical created identities. 'renameSession',
-- 'renameWindow' and 'setPaneTitle' perform explicit mutations
-- against generation-bound references. Earlier observations stay detached.
--
-- Operational failures use t'TmuxException'. 'tryTmux' catches that type only.
-- Cancellation retains its original exception class. If bounded cleanup
-- cannot finish, 'cleanupRecoveries' retrieves the owning recovery scope
-- from the exception context. A failed callback remains the primary failure.
module LibTmux.Server
  ( -- * Open and observe
    Server, ServerConfig (..), serverConfig, withServer, capture, serverGeneration
    -- * Start and retire a daemon
  , OwnedServerConfig (..), defaultOwnedServerConfig, withOwnedServer, killServer
    -- * Mutation deadlines
  , MutationOptions (..), defaultMutationOptions
    -- * Detached session creation
  , createSession, createSessionWith
    -- * Rename and title
  , renameSession, renameSessionWith, renameWindow, renameWindowWith, setPaneTitle, setPaneTitleWith
    -- * Shared ownership
  , Runtime, withRuntime, withServerIn
    -- * Operational failures
  , TmuxException (..), tryTmux
    -- * Scope cleanup
  , CleanupRecovery, CleanupStatus (..), cleanupRecoveries, cleanupFailure, cleanupObservation
  , inspectCleanup, resumeCleanup, awaitCleanup, detachUnresolved
    -- * Correlated capture recovery
  , CaptureRecovery, captureRecoveries, recoveryOperation, recoveryGeneration
  , ReadRecovery (..), inspectCaptureRecovery, resumeCaptureRecovery, detachCaptureRecovery
    -- * Correlated creation recovery
  , CreationRecovery, creationRecoveries, creationOperation, creationGeneration
  , creationReceipt, inspectCreationRecovery, resumeCreationRecovery, awaitCreationRecovery, detachCreationRecovery
    -- * Correlated mutation recovery
  , MutationRecovery, mutationRecoveries, mutationOperation, mutationGeneration
  , inspectMutationRecovery, resumeMutationRecovery, awaitMutationRecovery, detachMutationRecovery
  , Operation, Status (..), Stage (..), Outcome (..), operationStatus
  ) where

import Control.Concurrent.STM (atomically, readTVar, readTVarIO)
import Control.DeepSeq (force)
import Control.Exception

-- | One pinned endpoint and connection generation. Retaining this value after
-- 'withServer', 'withServerIn' or 'withOwnedServer' keeps no admission open.
data Server = Server !R.Runtime !R.ServerHandle !ByteString !Int !(IO ())

-- | Shared resource limits and cleanup ownership for Server handles. Create
-- one with 'withRuntime', then adopt endpoints through 'withServerIn'.
-- Detached t'Snapshot' values retain no Runtime.
newtype Runtime = Runtime R.Runtime

-- | Own a Runtime for the callback and perform bounded cleanup afterward.
-- Closing it retires every adopted handle; application-owned threads remain
-- the application's responsibility. Late adoption fails with 'RuntimeClosed'.
-- The daemon remains running.
--
-- Callback failures and cancellation keep their original exception class.
-- Incomplete cleanup retains a t'CleanupRecovery' in the exception context;
-- use 'tryTmux' and 'cleanupRecoveries' to keep that responsibility reachable.
withRuntime :: (Runtime -> IO a) -> IO a
withRuntime action = do
  runtime <- R.newRuntime P.normalFork
  Scope.runScope runtime (action (Runtime runtime))

-- | Adopt one endpoint within an existing Runtime and close only that handle
-- after the callback. Other handles remain admitted under the shared limits;
-- each adoption has its own 'serverGeneration'. Use 'withServer' for one handle.
-- Before the callback, opening refuses a daemon release older than 3.3a or an
-- unrecognized version reply. Opening also verifies the listener and holds a
-- process descriptor for 'killServer' where the host allows it (Linux 6.5 or
-- newer); the daemon's process ID is read without running a command hook. Where
-- that fails, the callback still runs and 'killServer' raises the failure.
--
-- Failed adoption can retain a t'CleanupRecovery' before a t'Server' exists.
-- Inspection, retry and waiting through that owner stay scoped to the failed
-- adoption. Cleanup preserves application exceptions, incoming masking state
-- and cancellation; known acquisition failures use t'TmuxException'.
withServerIn :: Runtime -> ServerConfig -> (Server -> IO a) -> IO a
withServerIn (Runtime runtime) config action = mask $ \restore -> do
  current <- atomically (R.usage runtime)
  when (not current.accepting) (throwIO RuntimeClosed)
  (executable, duration) <- restore (checkedConfiguration config)
  owner <- operational $
    catchNoPropagate (R.newServerOwner runtime) $
      \original@(ExceptionWithContext context (problem :: B.LimitError)) -> case problem of
        B.AdmissionClosed -> rethrowIO (ExceptionWithContext context RuntimeClosed)
        _ -> rethrowIO original
  Scope.runServerScope runtime owner $ restore $ do
    handle <- operational (R.adoptServerOwnerWith (\_ _ -> pure ()) runtime owner
      (posixBytes config.socketPath) (posixBytes config.pinDirectory))
    operational (qualifyVersion runtime handle executable duration)
    withAdoptedRetirement runtime handle executable duration $ \retire ->
      action (Server runtime handle executable duration retire)

-- | Pure configuration, checked when 'withServer' or 'withServerIn' opens the handle.
-- Paths retain POSIX bytes; no text decoding or shell interpretation occurs.
data ServerConfig = ServerConfig
  { socketPath :: !PosixPath -- ^ Existing tmux socket, with an absolute trusted path.
  , executable :: !PosixPath -- ^ Executable path or a program resolved once through PATH.
  , pinDirectory :: !PosixPath -- ^ Writable trusted directory on the socket's filesystem.
  , captureTimeout :: !NominalDiffTime -- ^ Capture and initial version-check deadline in seconds, positive and at most ten.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Configure an existing socket, resolving @tmux@ through PATH when opened.
-- The private pin uses the socket's parent directory. The capture timeout is
-- two seconds; callers can change it before opening a Server scope.
serverConfig :: PosixPath -> ServerConfig
serverConfig socket = ServerConfig socket (Os.fromBytestring "tmux") (Path.takeDirectory socket) 2

-- | Pin the endpoint, check the daemon release against the 3.3a admission
-- minimum, run the callback, then perform bounded owned cleanup. Version
-- observation runs no command hook, and neither does the process-ID read that
-- supports 'killServer'. A release older than 3.3a or an unrecognized reply
-- fails before entering the callback.
-- Cleanup never replaces a callback exception. Incomplete cleanup raises
-- 'CleanupFailed' after success, or annotates the original callback failure
-- with a reachable t'CleanupRecovery'. No daemon shutdown is requested.
withServer :: ServerConfig -> (Server -> IO a) -> IO a
withServer config action = do
  (executable, duration) <- checkedConfiguration config
  runtime <- R.newRuntime P.normalFork
  Scope.runScope runtime $ do
    handle <- operational (R.adopt runtime (posixBytes config.socketPath) (posixBytes config.pinDirectory))
    operational (qualifyVersion runtime handle executable duration)
    withAdoptedRetirement runtime handle executable duration $ \retire ->
      action (Server runtime handle executable duration retire)

qualifyVersion :: R.Runtime -> R.ServerHandle -> ByteString -> Int -> IO ()
qualifyVersion runtime handle executable duration = do
  (_, _, version) <- C.captureVersionWith P.defaultHooks runtime handle executable duration
  either (throwIO . UnsupportedTmuxVersion) (const (pure ())) (Version.requireSupported version)

checkedConfiguration :: ServerConfig -> IO (ByteString, Int)
checkedConfiguration config = checkedExecutable "captureTimeout" config.executable config.captureTimeout

-- | Validate a deadline, then resolve the executable; no external effect precedes either check.
checkedExecutable :: Text.Text -> PosixPath -> NominalDiffTime -> IO (ByteString, Int)
checkedExecutable field executable limit = do
  let seconds = toRational limit
  when (seconds <= 0 || seconds > 10) $
    throwIO (InvalidConfiguration (field <> " must be greater than zero and at most ten seconds"))
  resolved <- operational (resolveExecutable executable)
  pure (resolved, fromInteger (ceiling (seconds * 1000000)))

-- | Pure configuration for 'withOwnedServer', checked when its scope opens. The
-- socket is not configurable: the scope creates and removes its own.
data OwnedServerConfig = OwnedServerConfig
  { tmuxExecutable :: !PosixPath -- ^ Executable path or a program resolved once through PATH.
  , operationTimeout :: !NominalDiffTime -- ^ Version-check and 'capture' deadline in seconds, positive and at most ten.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Resolve @tmux@ through PATH, with a two-second 'operationTimeout'.
defaultOwnedServerConfig :: OwnedServerConfig
defaultOwnedServerConfig = OwnedServerConfig (Os.fromBytestring "tmux") 2

-- | Start a tmux daemon of its own, run the callback with a t'Server' for it,
-- then retire that daemon. The scope creates a private directory under @/tmp@
-- and the daemon's socket inside it; the caller supplies neither. Like
-- 'withServer', it refuses a release older than 3.3a before the callback. An
-- invalid configuration raises 'InvalidConfiguration' before any directory or
-- process exists.
--
-- On return, exception or cancellation the scope signals the original daemon
-- through a process descriptor and counts it as gone only when the descriptor
-- reports exit; a missing socket or finished client proves nothing. It then
-- removes the socket, lock file and directory it created. The callback keeps
-- the caller's masking state, and its result, exception or cancellation leaves
-- unchanged. A retained Server raises 'ServerClosed' afterwards.
--
-- A known startup failure raises 'OperationFailed'. Cleanup that fails after a
-- successful callback raises 'CleanupFailed', as 'withServer' does. If exit is
-- not observed within the bounded wait, the exception context keeps the owner
-- of the daemon and directory. Retrieve it with 'cleanupRecoveries', inspect
-- it with 'inspectCleanup', and retry bounded cleanup with 'resumeCleanup'.
-- 'awaitCleanup' waits on the daemon's process descriptor when one is held, or
-- on the start client's exit when not, then retries once. After a start that
-- found no listener it cannot wait for anything: the retry fails and the owner
-- stays, because no listener and a finished client do not prove the daemon gone.
-- Needs Linux 6.5 or newer. Panes receive SIGHUP; a background job started by
-- a hook can outlive the daemon.
withOwnedServer :: OwnedServerConfig -> (Server -> IO a) -> IO a
withOwnedServer config action = do
  (executable, duration) <- checkedExecutable "operationTimeout" config.tmuxExecutable config.operationTimeout
  lifecycle $ \tracked ->
    Owned.withOwnedServerWith Owned.defaultProbe {Owned.versionMicros = duration} executable $ \owned ->
      tracked (action (Server owned.runtime owned.handle executable duration
        (catchNoPropagate (Owned.settle owned.owner) (rethrowIO . Owned.annotated owned.owner))))

-- | Where the callback stood when a daemon-owning scope failed decides the public exception. A
-- callback failure stays primary. Cleanup that fails after the callback returned raises
-- 'CleanupFailed' with the owner's status and cause, as 'withServer' does; a failure before
-- the callback is an operational failure. Asynchronous exceptions keep their class throughout.
data Callback = NotEntered | Returned | Raised

lifecycle :: ((IO a -> IO a) -> IO a) -> IO a
lifecycle scope = do
  state <- newIORef NotEntered
  let tracked body = (body >>= \value -> value <$ writeIORef state Returned) `onException` writeIORef state Raised
  catchNoPropagate (scope tracked) $ \original -> do
    retained@(ExceptionWithContext context cause) <- Owned.promoteRecoveries original
    readIORef state >>= \case
      Raised -> rethrowIO retained
      Returned
        | isJust (fromException @SomeAsyncException cause) -> rethrowIO retained
        | recovery : _ <- cleanupRecoveries context ->
            rethrowIO (ExceptionWithContext context (toException (CleanupFailed (cleanupObservation recovery) (Just cause))))
      _ -> operationalFailure retained

-- | Hold a kill capability for the callback when the host and the listener allow one. Otherwise the
-- callback still runs, and 'killServer' raises the failure that prevented it.
withAdoptedRetirement :: R.Runtime -> R.ServerHandle -> ByteString -> Int -> (IO () -> IO a) -> IO a
withAdoptedRetirement runtime handle executable duration action =
  lifecycle $ \tracked ->
    Owned.withKillCapability Owned.defaultProbe {Owned.versionMicros = duration} executable runtime handle $ \admitted ->
      tracked (action (either throwIO retire admitted))
  where
    open = not <$> readTVarIO (R.serverPool handle).closing
    retire capability = do
      _ <- Owned.killAdoptedIf open capability
      report <- R.shutdownServerHandle runtime handle
      unless (null report.pending && null report.readWorkers && null report.closeFailures)
        (throwIO (Owned.CleanupPending (show report)))
      remaining <- atomically $ do
        forM_ report.unresolved (R.detachOperation runtime . fst)
        (.unresolved) <$> R.inspectServerHandle runtime handle
      unless (null remaining) (throwIO (Owned.OperationsUnresolved (length remaining)))

-- | Retire the daemon behind an adopted Server and return after its exit is
-- observed through a process descriptor. The descriptor comes from the pinned
-- socket when the Server is admitted, and the daemon's reported process ID must
-- match it. Retirement needs no tmux response or command lane. A socket rebound
-- after adoption refuses instead of stopping another server. Later operations
-- raise 'ServerClosed', and so does a call that arrives after the adopting
-- scope's callback has left; a call admitted before that finishes. Interrupted
-- cleanup keeps a t'CleanupRecovery'; known failures raise 'OperationFailed',
-- including the failure that prevented holding the descriptor at admission.
-- Needs Linux 6.5 or newer.
killServer :: Server -> IO ()
killServer (Server _ handle _ _ retire) = operational $ do
  closed <- atomically (readTVar (R.serverPool handle).closing)
  when closed (throwIO ServerClosed)
  catchNoPropagate retire (\problem -> Owned.promoteRecoveries problem >>= rethrowIO)

-- | Acquire the complete baseline graph, metadata and attached clients.
-- Returned values own their data and remain usable after 'withServer' exits.
-- Capacity and acquisition failure are errors; they never become empty lists.
capture :: Server -> IO Snapshot
capture (Server runtime handle executable duration _) = operational $ do
  closed <- atomically (readTVar (R.serverPool handle).closing)
  when closed (throwIO ServerClosed)
  (started, finished, decoded) <- C.captureSnapshot runtime handle executable duration
  stamped <- either (throwIO . InvalidObservation . Text.pack . show) pure
    (G.stampSnapshot started finished decoded)
  evaluate (force stamped)

-- | The handle's opaque generation, available without contacting tmux.
serverGeneration :: Server -> Generation
serverGeneration (Server _ handle _ _ _) = Pin.pinGeneration (R.serverPin handle)

-- | Per-command deadline, checked before admission. Start from
-- 'defaultMutationOptions' and update 'timeout' in seconds.
data MutationOptions = MutationOptions
  { timeout :: !NominalDiffTime -- ^ Positive seconds, at most ten; the default is one.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | One second for command submission and its complete response.
defaultMutationOptions :: MutationOptions
defaultMutationOptions = MutationOptions 1

-- | Create a detached session through this pinned Server. Start from
-- 'LibTmux.Creation.defaultSessionOptions'. The result contains actual created refs,
-- not observed records; capture again before inspecting the new graph.
-- After-hooks may already have renamed or destroyed these targets.
createSession :: Server -> Creation.SessionOptions -> IO Creation.CreatedSession
createSession = createSessionWith defaultMutationOptions

-- | Create with one 'timeout' covering caller-context acquisition, admission
-- and completion. 'MutationAppliedWithErrors', cancellation and timeout may
-- retain a t'CreationRecovery' with known IDs. A missing receipt proves no
-- absence. Creation never retries and never starts a replacement daemon.
-- Oversized options raise 'InvalidMutationArgument' before admission. A caller
-- environment beyond the native launch budget raises 'InvalidConfiguration'
-- without admitting an operation.
createSessionWith :: MutationOptions -> Server -> Creation.SessionOptions -> IO Creation.CreatedSession
createSessionWith options (Server runtime handle executable _ _) settings = operational $ do
  duration <- mutationDuration options
  closed <- atomically (readTVar (R.serverPool handle).closing)
  when closed (throwIO ServerClosed)
  Create.performCreation P.defaultHooks duration runtime handle executable settings

-- | Rename the session targeted by a reference from this Server generation.
-- The name is literal text. Earlier t'Snapshot' values keep their old names;
-- call 'capture' for a new observation. Use 'renameSessionWith' for a deadline.
renameSession :: Server -> SessionRef -> Text.Text -> IO ()
renameSession = renameSessionWith defaultMutationOptions

-- | 'renameSession' with an explicit 'timeout'. A known primary rejection raises
-- 'MutationRejected'; an applied command with a failed hook raises
-- 'MutationAppliedWithErrors'. Neither result implies rollback.
renameSessionWith :: MutationOptions -> Server -> SessionRef -> Text.Text -> IO ()
renameSessionWith options server (G.SessionRef generation ident) label =
  mutate options server generation (Command.RenameSession ident label)

-- | Rename one physical window across all its session links. The label retains
-- bytes through t'TmuxText'; tmux may reject names its release does not accept.
-- Format-looking text stays literal. See 'renameWindowWith' for a deadline.
renameWindow :: Server -> WindowRef -> TmuxText -> IO ()
renameWindow = renameWindowWith defaultMutationOptions

-- | 'renameWindow' with an explicit deadline. Success confirms the primary
-- command's response, not completion of background jobs started by hooks.
-- 'capture' observes the current label; existing snapshots remain detached.
renameWindowWith :: MutationOptions -> Server -> WindowRef -> TmuxText -> IO ()
renameWindowWith options server (G.WindowRef generation ident) label =
  mutate options server generation (Command.RenameWindow ident label)

-- | Set the literal title of a pane from this Server generation. The pane's
-- application can replace it later. Use 'setPaneTitleWith' for a deadline.
setPaneTitle :: Server -> PaneRef -> Text.Text -> IO ()
setPaneTitle = setPaneTitleWith defaultMutationOptions

-- | 'setPaneTitle' with an explicit deadline. Missing panes fail with
-- 'MutationRejected'. Foreign and offline references fail with 'InvalidTarget'
-- before dispatch. No mutation retries after cancellation or timeout.
setPaneTitleWith :: MutationOptions -> Server -> PaneRef -> Text.Text -> IO ()
setPaneTitleWith options server (G.PaneRef generation ident) label =
  mutate options server generation (Command.SetPaneTitle ident label)

mutate :: MutationOptions -> Server -> Generation -> Command.Mutation -> IO ()
mutate options server@(Server runtime handle executable _ _) generation command = operational $ do
  duration <- mutationDuration options
  closed <- atomically (readTVar (R.serverPool handle).closing)
  when closed (throwIO ServerClosed)
  unless (generation == serverGeneration server)
    (throwIO (InvalidTarget "reference belongs to a different Server generation or an offline fixture"))
  M.performMutation P.defaultHooks duration runtime handle executable command

mutationDuration :: MutationOptions -> IO Int
mutationDuration options = do
  let seconds = toRational options.timeout
  when (seconds <= 0 || seconds > 10)
    (throwIO (InvalidConfiguration "mutation timeout must be positive and at most ten seconds"))
  pure (fromInteger (ceiling (seconds * 1000000)))

-- | Correlated creation owners from 'tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'. Keep the
-- context when handling failure, including an applied command's hook error.
creationRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CreationRecovery]
creationRecoveries = Context.getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only identity of the original creation operation.
creationOperation :: CreationRecovery -> Operation
creationOperation = R.receiptOperation . Create.recoveryReceipt

-- | Originating Server generation, including after the scope closes.
creationGeneration :: CreationRecovery -> Generation
creationGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . Create.recoveryReceipt

-- | Read any complete historical receipt already observed by the library.
-- This reads owned metadata without contacting tmux. 'Nothing' does not mean
-- no session was created; unread or incomplete evidence cannot supply IDs.
creationReceipt :: CreationRecovery -> IO (Maybe Creation.CreatedSession)
creationReceipt = atomically . Create.observedReceipt

-- | Inspect logical outcome and native ownership without external operations.
inspectCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectCreationRecovery = atomically . Create.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing cleanup; never execute the creation again.
resumeCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ()
resumeCreationRecovery = operational . Create.resumeRecovery

-- | Join the original native child and decoder. Logical uncertainty can
-- remain, and this wait proves no hook/background-job completion.
awaitCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
awaitCreationRecovery = operational . Create.awaitRecovery

-- | Relinquish logical uncertainty while preserving physical cleanup owners.
-- This does not remove the created session or repeat the command.
detachCreationRecovery :: CreationRecovery -> IO Bool
detachCreationRecovery = operational . atomically . Create.detachRecovery

-- | Catch library failures with their exception context. Retain this value
-- when handling an error so cleanup and operation owners stay reachable.
-- Application exceptions and asynchronous cancellation propagate.
tryTmux :: IO a -> IO (Either (ExceptionWithContext TmuxException) a)
tryTmux = tryWithContext

-- | Cleanup owners retained by a failed or cancelled scope. The context
-- comes from 'tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'. Inspection performs no tmux IO.
-- Nested scopes can contribute overlapping owners; inspect and resume each
-- retained responsibility through 'inspectCleanup' and 'resumeCleanup'.
cleanupRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CleanupRecovery]
cleanupRecoveries = Context.getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Relinquish one logical operation from this cleanup scope. This releases
-- no native resources and does not prove that daemon-side work completed.
detachUnresolved :: CleanupRecovery -> Operation -> IO Bool
detachUnresolved recovery = operational . Scope.detachUnresolved recovery

-- | Read owners retained by a capture or Server version check, including cancellation.
captureRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [CaptureRecovery]
captureRecoveries = Context.getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only operation identity for the failed capture.
recoveryOperation :: CaptureRecovery -> Operation
recoveryOperation = R.receiptOperation . C.recoveryReceipt

-- | Correlate the failed capture with its Server generation.
recoveryGeneration :: CaptureRecovery -> Generation
recoveryGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . C.recoveryReceipt

-- | Observe logical outcome, decoder ownership and native cleanup locally.
-- This reads runtime metadata and performs no tmux command.
inspectCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectCaptureRecovery = atomically . C.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing cleanup without dispatching the capture again.
resumeCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO ()
resumeCaptureRecovery = operational . C.resumeRecovery

-- | Explicitly detach logical uncertainty while preserving native ownership.
detachCaptureRecovery :: CaptureRecovery -> IO Bool
detachCaptureRecovery = operational . atomically . C.detachRecovery

-- | Recover the exact operation after failure, timeout or cancellation. The
-- context comes from 'tryTmux' or 'tryWithContext'; cancellation keeps its
-- original exception class and is not caught by 'tryTmux'.
mutationRecoveries :: ExceptionContext -> [MutationRecovery]
mutationRecoveries = Context.getExceptionAnnotations

-- | Metadata-only identity of the original command. 'operationStatus' remains
-- available after native cleanup; this value contains no command operands.
mutationOperation :: MutationRecovery -> Operation
mutationOperation = R.receiptOperation . M.recoveryReceipt

-- | Server generation associated with this mutation's recovery owner.
mutationGeneration :: MutationRecovery -> Generation
mutationGeneration = R.receiptGeneration . M.recoveryReceipt

-- | Inspect the original operation's logical and physical ownership locally.
-- This performs no tmux command. An unknown outcome does not become success
-- merely because the native child has exited.
inspectMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
inspectMutationRecovery = atomically . M.inspectRecovery

-- | Resume existing native cleanup and decoder ownership, without repeating
-- the command. Allocation failure retains the same recovery owner.
resumeMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ()
resumeMutationRecovery = operational . M.resumeRecovery

-- | Wait for the original decoder and native child to retire. This may still
-- return retained 'OutcomeUnknown'; it does not wait for a daemon hook job.
-- Cancellation keeps this recovery owner in the new exception context.
awaitMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO ReadRecovery
awaitMutationRecovery = operational . M.awaitRecovery

-- | Relinquish this operation's logical uncertainty. This neither cancels
-- daemon work nor releases native resources, and never repeats the mutation.
detachMutationRecovery :: MutationRecovery -> IO Bool
detachMutationRecovery = operational . atomically . M.detachRecovery

-- | Read retained operation metadata, including after its physical cleanup.
operationStatus :: Operation -> IO Status
operationStatus = atomically . S.status

resolveExecutable :: PosixPath -> IO ByteString
resolveExecutable executable = case Platform.coercionToPlatformTypes of
  Left _ -> throwIO (InvalidConfiguration "this package requires Linux POSIX paths")
  Right (_, proof) -> do
    selected <- Directory.findExecutable (coerceWith (sym proof) executable)
    path <- maybe (throwIO (InvalidConfiguration "tmux executable was not found")) Directory.makeAbsolute selected
    pure (posixBytes (coerceWith proof path))

posixBytes :: PosixPath -> ByteString
posixBytes = Bytes.pack . map (fromIntegral . fromEnum . Os.toChar) . Os.unpack

operational :: IO a -> IO a
operational action = catchNoPropagate action operationalFailure

-- | Wrap a known backend failure, keeping its context; application exceptions and cancellation pass through.
operationalFailure :: ExceptionWithContext SomeException -> IO a
operationalFailure original@(ExceptionWithContext context problem) =
  let known = or
        [ isJust (fromException @IOException problem)
        , isJust (fromException @Pin.PinError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @R.ReadError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @C.CaptureError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @B.LimitError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @P.OwnerError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @N.Failure problem)
        , isJust (fromException @S.AdmissionError problem)
        , isJust (fromException @Owned.OwnedError problem)
        ]
  in if known && not (isJust (fromException @SomeAsyncException problem))
       then rethrowIO (ExceptionWithContext context (OperationFailed problem))
       else rethrowIO original

-- | Detached tmux observations and pure navigation.
--
-- "LibTmux.Server" acquires a t'Snapshot' in IO. Every operation in this
-- module reads owned Haskell values, including after the Server closes.
-- Use ordinary lists, comprehensions and folds for application predicates.
--
-- t'Window' and t'Pane' are physical entities. A t'WindowLink' identifies an
-- observed session/index/window binding; t'PaneOccurrence' retains that
-- context. 'paneOccurrences' therefore preserves repeated appearances while
-- 'panes' lists each physical pane once.
--
-- References compare identity within one Server generation. A lookup reads
-- the supplied snapshot, including a newer snapshot from that same Server.
-- Independent Server scopes have different generations. Resolve an ID again
-- with 'lookupPaneId' when deliberately selecting a newly observed entity.
--
-- Observation fields are exported for record dot and local updates. Editing
-- a record does not change a snapshot's indexes or establish provenance.
-- "LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture" constructs validated offline snapshots;
-- 'snapshotOrigin' distinguishes them from observations acquired through IO.
module LibTmux.Snapshot
  ( -- * Complete observations
    Snapshot, ServerInfo (..), SnapshotOrigin (..), snapshotOrigin
  , serverInfo, captureInterval, CaptureInterval (..)
    -- * Physical and contextual values
  , Session (..), Window (..), Pane (..), WindowLink (..), PaneOccurrence (..)
  , Client (..), ClientAttachment (..)
    -- * Target identity
  , Generation, SessionRef, WindowRef, PaneRef
  , sessionId, windowId, paneId
    -- * Ordered sources
  , sessions, windows, panes, windowLinks, paneOccurrences, clients
    -- * Indexed navigation
  , LookupError (..), lookupSession, lookupWindow, lookupPane
  , linksForSession, panesForWindow
  , lookupSessionId, lookupWindowId, lookupPaneId
    -- * Lossless labels
  , TmuxText, labelFromBytes, labelBytes, labelText
  ) where

import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text.Encoding.Error (UnicodeException)
import LibTmux.Id (PaneId, SessionId, WindowId)
import LibTmux.Internal.Graph
  ( Snapshot, ServerInfo (..), CaptureInterval (..), captureInterval, serverInfo, clients
  , Session (..), Window (..), Pane (..), WindowLink (..), PaneOccurrence (..)
  , Client (..), ClientAttachment (..)
  , Generation, SessionRef, WindowRef, PaneRef, LookupError (..)
  )
import LibTmux.Internal.Graph qualified as G
import LibTmux.Internal.TmuxText (TmuxText)
import LibTmux.Internal.TmuxText qualified as Label

-- | Where the validated values were obtained. A server capture does not
-- establish current liveness. Offline namespaces carry no targeting authority.
data SnapshotOrigin
  = AcquiredFromTmux -- ^ Acquired through an operational Server handle.
  | DefinedOffline !Text -- ^ Constructed and validated in a named fixture namespace.
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

-- | Inspect provenance without contacting tmux. See
-- "LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture" for validated offline construction.
snapshotOrigin :: Snapshot -> SnapshotOrigin
snapshotOrigin snapshot = case (G.serverInfo snapshot).generation of
  G.Generation {} -> AcquiredFromTmux
  G.FixtureGeneration name -> DefinedOffline name

-- | Native session ID, without the reference's generation guarantee.
sessionId :: SessionRef -> SessionId
sessionId (G.SessionRef _ ident) = ident

-- | Native physical window ID. Window-link indices are separate values.
windowId :: WindowRef -> WindowId
windowId (G.WindowRef _ ident) = ident

-- | Native pane ID. Comparing IDs alone does not compare Server identity.
paneId :: PaneRef -> PaneId
paneId (G.PaneRef _ ident) = ident

-- | Physical sessions in numeric ID order.
sessions :: Snapshot -> [Session]
sessions = G.graphSessions . G.entities

-- | Physical windows in numeric ID order, independent of their links.
windows :: Snapshot -> [Window]
windows = G.graphWindows . G.entities

-- | Physical panes in numeric ID order. Use 'paneOccurrences' for link context.
panes :: Snapshot -> [Pane]
panes = G.graphPanes . G.entities

-- | Window appearances in session ID and window-index order.
windowLinks :: Snapshot -> [WindowLink]
windowLinks = G.graphLinks . G.entities

-- | Every pane appearance, ordered by link and then pane index.
paneOccurrences :: Snapshot -> [PaneOccurrence]
paneOccurrences = G.graphOccurrences . G.entities

-- | Resolve a session in this snapshot. Missing and foreign refs are errors.
lookupSession :: Snapshot -> SessionRef -> Either LookupError Session
lookupSession snapshot = G.lookupSession (G.entities snapshot)

-- | Resolve the supplied generation's physical window in this snapshot.
lookupWindow :: Snapshot -> WindowRef -> Either LookupError Window
lookupWindow snapshot = G.lookupWindow (G.entities snapshot)

-- | Resolve the supplied generation's physical pane in this snapshot.
lookupPane :: Snapshot -> PaneRef -> Either LookupError Pane
lookupPane snapshot = G.lookupPane (G.entities snapshot)

-- | A session's window links in window-index order, preserving repeated windows.
linksForSession :: Snapshot -> SessionRef -> Either LookupError [WindowLink]
linksForSession snapshot = G.linksForSession (G.entities snapshot)

-- | A physical window's panes in pane-index order, then numeric ID order.
panesForWindow :: Snapshot -> WindowRef -> Either LookupError [Pane]
panesForWindow snapshot = G.panesForWindow (G.entities snapshot)

-- | Select the session currently observed under an ID in this snapshot.
-- This creates no continuity guarantee with a previously opened Server.
lookupSessionId :: Snapshot -> SessionId -> Either LookupError Session
lookupSessionId snapshot ident = lookupSession snapshot (G.SessionRef (serverInfo snapshot).generation ident)

-- | Select the physical window observed under an ID in this snapshot.
lookupWindowId :: Snapshot -> WindowId -> Either LookupError Window
lookupWindowId snapshot ident = lookupWindow snapshot (G.WindowRef (serverInfo snapshot).generation ident)

-- | Select the pane observed under an ID in this snapshot.
lookupPaneId :: Snapshot -> PaneId -> Either LookupError Pane
lookupPaneId snapshot ident = lookupPane snapshot (G.PaneRef (serverInfo snapshot).generation ident)

-- | Copy bytes into an owned label. This performs no encoding replacement.
labelFromBytes :: ByteString -> TmuxText
labelFromBytes = Label.fromBytes

-- | Exact bytes reported by tmux, after transport decoding.
labelBytes :: TmuxText -> ByteString
labelBytes = Label.toBytes

-- | Decode a label as UTF-8, retaining byte access on failure.
labelText :: TmuxText -> Either UnicodeException Text
labelText = Label.decodeUtf8

-- | Build validated detached snapshots for pure application tests.
--
-- No operation in this module contacts tmux. Named fixture references can
-- model successive observations; they never equal a live Server generation.
-- Snapshot and live-reference constructors remain hidden.
-- Validation checks graph and metadata laws; wire decoding, tmux normalization
-- and transport limits belong to acquisition rather than fixture construction.
--
-- Start with 'fixtureOrigin' and 'emptyFixture', construct ordinary observation
-- records using this module's reference builders, then call 'validateFixture'.
module LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture
  ( -- * Offline identity
    FixtureOrigin, fixtureOrigin, fixtureGeneration, sessionRef, windowRef, paneRef
    -- * Complete fixture inputs
  , Fixture (..), AttachedClient (..), emptyFixture
    -- * Validation
  , FixtureError (..), validateFixture
  ) where

import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux.Id (PaneId, SessionId, WindowId)
import LibTmux.Internal.Graph qualified as G
import LibTmux.Snapshot
  ( Generation, Snapshot, ServerInfo (..), Session, SessionRef, Window, WindowRef
  , Pane, PaneRef, WindowLink
  )
import LibTmux.Value (WindowIndex)
import LibTmux.Version (TmuxVersion)
import System.OsPath.Posix (PosixPath)
import System.OsString.Posix (PosixString)
import System.OsString.Posix qualified as Os

-- | A named offline namespace. Equal names deliberately compare equal, so
-- tests can model successive observations. This cannot represent a Server.
newtype FixtureOrigin = FixtureOrigin Generation
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

-- | Select a pure fixture namespace. No endpoint lookup or random IO occurs.
fixtureOrigin :: Text -> FixtureOrigin
fixtureOrigin = FixtureOrigin . G.FixtureGeneration

-- | The offline generation for t'Fixture' metadata. Replacing it with a connection
-- generation causes 'validateFixture' to reject the metadata.
fixtureGeneration :: FixtureOrigin -> Generation
fixtureGeneration (FixtureOrigin generation) = generation

-- | Construct a session reference that belongs only to this offline origin.
sessionRef :: FixtureOrigin -> SessionId -> SessionRef
sessionRef origin = G.SessionRef (fixtureGeneration origin)

-- | Construct a physical window reference without granting live authority.
windowRef :: FixtureOrigin -> WindowId -> WindowRef
windowRef origin = G.WindowRef (fixtureGeneration origin)

-- | Construct a pane reference without consulting or targeting a daemon.
paneRef :: FixtureOrigin -> PaneId -> PaneRef
paneRef origin = G.PaneRef (fixtureGeneration origin)

-- | Ordinary finite inputs. Validation applies the captured graph's laws;
-- record construction or updates alone do not establish those laws.
data Fixture = Fixture
  { info :: !ServerInfo -- ^ Synthetic metadata in the supplied offline generation.
  , sessions :: ![Session] -- ^ Physical sessions, with references from this origin.
  , windows :: ![Window] -- ^ Physical windows, independent of contextual appearances.
  , panes :: ![Pane] -- ^ Physical panes with their containing window references.
  , windowLinks :: ![WindowLink] -- ^ Session/index/window appearances, including active selections.
  , clients :: ![AttachedClient] -- ^ Complete attached-client listing for this fixture.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | An attached client's native identity and context before graph validation.
-- Validation resolves its values from the same snapshot; it never trusts a
-- caller-supplied nested attachment record.
data AttachedClient = AttachedClient
  { name :: !PosixString -- ^ Nonempty reported client-name bytes.
  , pid :: !Integer -- ^ Positive synthetic client PID in the native PID range.
  , tty :: !(Maybe PosixPath) -- ^ Nonempty terminal path when provided.
  , session :: !SessionId -- ^ Attachment session ID.
  , window :: !WindowId -- ^ Selected physical window ID.
  , index :: !WindowIndex -- ^ Selected window-link index in the attachment session.
  , pane :: !PaneId -- ^ The selected physical pane, not an independent client focus.
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Empty complete inputs with explicit synthetic metadata: PID 1, epoch 0
-- and path @fixture:offline@. No process or socket exists by implication.
-- The version and every edited field are checked by 'validateFixture'.
emptyFixture :: FixtureOrigin -> TmuxVersion -> Fixture
emptyFixture origin version = Fixture
  (ServerInfo (fixtureGeneration origin) 1 0 version (Os.fromBytestring "fixture:offline"))
  [] [] [] [] []

-- | A failed graph or complete-snapshot validation, with domain
-- context from the validator. Failed input never becomes an empty snapshot.
data FixtureError
  = InvalidGraph !Text -- ^ Invalid references, multiplicity, attachment counts or selections.
  | InvalidSnapshot !Text -- ^ Invalid metadata or attached-client context.
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Validate and force owned values using the capture graph's invariants.
-- Successful fixtures have no acquisition interval and carry offline
-- provenance. Their references cannot equal references from a Server scope.
validateFixture :: FixtureOrigin -> Fixture -> Either FixtureError Snapshot
validateFixture origin input = do
  graph <- first (InvalidGraph . Text.pack . show) $
    G.assembleEntityGraph (fixtureGeneration origin)
      input.sessions input.windows input.panes input.windowLinks
  let clients =
        [ G.ClientInput row.name row.pid row.tty row.session row.window row.index row.pane
        | row <- input.clients
        ]
  first (InvalidSnapshot . Text.pack . show) (G.assembleSnapshot input.info graph clients)

-- | Positive dimensions and nonnegative contextual indices.
--
-- Construction and access are pure. Window-link indices and pane indices
-- have distinct types; neither substitutes for an entity ID. A constructor
-- checks the mathematical domain, while command-specific limits belong at
-- the operation boundary. Use 'mkDimension', 'mkWindowIndex' and 'mkPaneIndex'
-- to validate input; their accessors return mathematical integers. Entity
-- identifiers belong to "LibTmux.Id".
--
-- >>> fmap dimensionValue (mkDimension 120)
-- Right 120
-- >>> mkDimension 0
-- Left (NonPositiveDimension 0)
module LibTmux.Value
  ( -- * Checked types
    Dimension
  , WindowIndex
  , PaneIndex
    -- * Validate input
  , ValueError (..)
  , mkDimension
  , mkWindowIndex
  , mkPaneIndex
    -- * Read numeric values
  , dimensionValue
  , windowIndexValue
  , paneIndexValue
  ) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData)

-- | Positive cells, constructed with 'mkDimension'. Command and field limits
-- are checked separately. Compare dimensions directly or use 'dimensionValue'
-- with an integer literal.
newtype Dimension = Dimension Integer
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | Nonnegative index of a window link within a session, not a physical window ID.
-- Construct with 'mkWindowIndex'; read with 'windowIndexValue'.
newtype WindowIndex = WindowIndex Integer
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | Nonnegative pane index within a window, not a pane ID.
-- Construct with 'mkPaneIndex'; read with 'paneIndexValue'.
newtype PaneIndex = PaneIndex Integer
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)
  deriving newtype (NFData)

-- | A scalar outside its mathematical domain.
data ValueError
  = NonPositiveDimension !Integer -- ^ The supplied dimension was zero or negative.
  | NegativeIndex !Integer -- ^ The supplied contextual index was negative.
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Construct a positive dimension without applying a command-specific maximum.
mkDimension :: Integer -> Either ValueError Dimension
mkDimension value
  | value > 0 = Right (Dimension value)
  | otherwise = Left (NonPositiveDimension value)

-- | Construct a nonnegative window-link index.
mkWindowIndex :: Integer -> Either ValueError WindowIndex
mkWindowIndex value
  | value >= 0 = Right (WindowIndex value)
  | otherwise = Left (NegativeIndex value)

-- | Construct a nonnegative pane index.
mkPaneIndex :: Integer -> Either ValueError PaneIndex
mkPaneIndex value
  | value >= 0 = Right (PaneIndex value)
  | otherwise = Left (NegativeIndex value)

-- | Read a dimension as a mathematical integer, without narrowing conversion.
dimensionValue :: Dimension -> Integer
dimensionValue (Dimension value) = value

-- | Read a window-link index as a mathematical integer.
windowIndexValue :: WindowIndex -> Integer
windowIndexValue (WindowIndex value) = value

-- | Read a pane index as a mathematical integer.
paneIndexValue :: PaneIndex -> Integer
paneIndexValue (PaneIndex value) = value

-- | Parse and order tmux release identities, and check the minimum release.
--
-- These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute @tmux -V@
-- nor contact a server. Admission is a floor: every release at or above
-- 3.3a passes, with no upper bound. Admission says nothing about which
-- releases the project has tested, and individual features still need
-- capability and conformance checks.
--
-- Use 'parseVersion' for input, 'requireSupported' for minimum-version
-- admission and 'renderVersion' for the spelling tmux reports.
--
-- >>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
-- >>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported)
-- Right "3.3a"
--
-- Numeric components compare as numbers, and a patch letter follows its
-- release:
--
-- >>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.9" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
-- Right True
-- >>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10a"
-- Right True
--
-- A development build or release candidate ranks below the release it
-- precedes:
--
-- >>> (<) <$> parseVersion "next-3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10-rc"
-- Right True
-- >>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10-rc2" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
-- Right True
module LibTmux.Version
  ( -- * Release identity and errors
    TmuxVersion
  , VersionError (..)
    -- * Parse and render
  , parseVersion
  , renderVersion
    -- * Admit a release
  , requireSupported
  ) where

import Control.DeepSeq (NFData (rnf))
import Control.Monad (guard)
import Data.Maybe (fromMaybe)
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import Text.Read (readMaybe)

-- | A tmux release, release candidate or development build, constructed by
-- 'parseVersion' and rendered by 'renderVersion'. Ordering compares the numeric
-- components, then @next-X.Y < X.Y-rc < X.Y-rcN < X.Y < X.Ya@. Rendering
-- reproduces the accepted spelling, so @X.Y-rc@ and @X.Y-rc1@ are distinct.
data TmuxVersion = TmuxVersion !Integer !Integer !Stage
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

instance NFData TmuxVersion where
  rnf (TmuxVersion major minor stage) = rnf major `seq` rnf minor `seq` rnf stage

-- | Position within one numeric release. Constructor order is ascending rank.
data Stage
  = Development -- ^ @next-X.Y@, the development line before @X.Y@.
  | Candidate !(Maybe Integer)
    -- ^ @X.Y-rc@, an unnumbered candidate, or @X.Y-rcN@.
  | Release -- ^ @X.Y@.
  | Patch !Char -- ^ @X.Ya@, a lowercase patch letter.
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

instance NFData Stage where
  rnf Development = ()
  rnf (Candidate number) = rnf number
  rnf Release = ()
  rnf (Patch letter) = rnf letter

-- | Invalid release syntax or a release below the supported minimum.
data VersionError
  = MalformedVersion !Text -- ^ Bounded copy of input that is not a tmux release identity.
  | UnsupportedVersion !TmuxVersion -- ^ A release older than 3.3a.
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

-- | Parse a release identity or the output of @tmux -V@, allowing a leading
-- @tmux @ and one final LF. The accepted forms are @X.Y@, @X.Ya@, @X.Y-rc@,
-- @X.Y-rcN@ and @next-X.Y@. Unknown suffixes, including a bare @master@, are
-- rejected rather than assigned a guessed release. Diagnostics retain at most
-- 64 chars.
parseVersion :: Text -> Either VersionError TmuxVersion
parseVersion input
  | Text.length input > 64 = invalid
  | otherwise = maybe invalid Right parsed
  where
    invalid = Left (MalformedVersion (Text.copy (Text.take 64 input)))
    line = fromMaybe input (Text.stripSuffix "\n" input)
    body = fromMaybe line (Text.stripPrefix "tmux " line)
    parsed = case Text.stripPrefix "next-" body of
      Just core -> do
        (major, minor, rest) <- components core
        guard (Text.null rest)
        pure (TmuxVersion major minor Development)
      Nothing -> do
        (major, minor, rest) <- components body
        TmuxVersion major minor <$> stage rest

    components value = do
      let (majorText, rest) = Text.breakOn "." value
      afterDot <- Text.stripPrefix "." rest
      let (minorText, suffixText) = Text.span asciiDigit afterDot
      major <- number majorText
      minor <- number minorText
      pure (major, minor, suffixText)

    stage suffix = case Text.unpack suffix of
      [] -> Just Release
      [c] | c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' -> Just (Patch c)
      _ | Just digits <- Text.stripPrefix "-rc" suffix -> candidate digits
      _ -> Nothing

    candidate digits
      | Text.null digits = Just (Candidate Nothing)
      | otherwise = do
          count <- number digits
          guard (count > 0)
          pure (Candidate (Just count))

    number value = case Text.uncons value of
      Nothing -> Nothing
      Just ('0', remaining) | not (Text.null remaining) -> Nothing
      Just _ | Text.all asciiDigit value -> readMaybe (Text.unpack value)
      _ -> Nothing

    asciiDigit c = c >= '0' && c <= '9'

-- | Render the release as tmux spells it, without the executable name or
-- newline. Parsing the result returns an equal value.
renderVersion :: TmuxVersion -> Text
renderVersion (TmuxVersion major minor stage) = case stage of
  Development -> "next-" <> numbers
  Candidate count -> numbers <> "-rc" <> maybe "" (Text.pack . show) count
  Release -> numbers
  Patch letter -> numbers <> Text.singleton letter
  where
    numbers = Text.pack (show major <> "." <> show minor)

-- | Admit every release at or above 3.3a, including intermediate releases,
-- newer releases and the development builds and candidates ranked above it.
-- Plain 3.3 and older releases fail. The check has no upper bound, so passing
-- it does not mean the project tested that release. Individual features need
-- their own capability checks; passing this check does not qualify an entire
-- release.
requireSupported :: TmuxVersion -> Either VersionError TmuxVersion
requireSupported version
  | version < TmuxVersion 3 3 (Patch 'a') = Left (UnsupportedVersion version)
  | otherwise = Right version
